newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Jan producer inflation at 18-month high.
newsitem.headline: S.African Jan producer inflation at 18-month high.

text.p: South African producer inflation rose to its highest level in eighteen months when it rose 9.2 percent year-on-year in January, the Central Statistical Service (CSS) said on Thursday.
It said the rise was the highest since June 1995 when the producer price index rose 10.5 percent year-on-year.

The local production component of the index rose 0.9 percent month-on-month and 9.2 percent year-on-year, while the imported component grew 0.6 percent from December and 9.6 percent from January 1996.

CSS said the main reasons for the increase in the local component were a 3.0 percent increase in wood and wood product prices, a 3.1 percent increase in paper and paper product prices and 3.9 percent growth in electricity prices.
Footwear prices rose 2.5 percent, petroleum and coal 1.9 percent, tobacco products 1.5 percent and mining and quarrying product prices were up 1.7 percent.

The imported component was elevated by a 9.5 percent increase in metal product prices, 5.2 percent growth in paper and paper product prices and a 2.3 percent rise in mining and quarrying product prices.

The CSS added that the distribution of item-prices collected for imported commodities was being reviewed to ensure that the number of data points gathered was in better proportion to the weights of the relative categories.

"Provided that importers are helpful with the requisite information, there should therefore be an improvement in future in the availability of price data of comparable items with which price changes can be monitored," it said.
